_what: Every account decomposed into the same five fields: identifier, fiduciary, servicer, debt_holder, benefit. No special cases - a passport and a prepaid card are read the same way, and if one of them needs a rule of its own then the model is wrong rather than the account.
_the_label_is_not_a_layer: `label` records what the thing is CALLED and is never consulted when the layers are read. A product named 'trust' whose funding obligation never transferred is a custodial arrangement with a trust-shaped name. Calling something a trust does not move a duty; only an instrument does.
_evidence_states: Every layer carries one: cited (a statute, regulation or instruction is named), stated_by_principal (he told us, and that is recorded as its own kind of evidence), unverified (NOBODY HAS CHECKED - not a guess, a gap), not_applicable (the layer genuinely does not exist for this account).
_why_unverified_stays_unverified: The whole point of the trace is to find who carries the obligation. A plausible guess in debt_holder is the one field somebody would act on, so it is left empty and marked. An account map that invents a debt-holder is worse than one that admits it does not know.
_versioning: Each entry carries its own version and the authority it was read from. When a statute or instruction changes, the ENTRY changes - core/account_model.py does not.

us_passport.label: United States passport

identifier.note: The Secretary of State issues passports; the number identifies the document, not an account.

holder.note: A passport creates no payment obligation, so there is no interest for anybody to hold and none to enforce. Same reasoning as the fiduciary and debt_holder layers here: definitional from what the statute authorises, not a gap somebody failed to fill.

fiduciary.note: A passport is a travel document and a claim of nationality. Nobody holds it in trust for anyone - there is no res and no beneficiary, so this layer genuinely does not exist rather than being unknown.

debt_holder.note: No obligation is created by holding one. The fee is paid at issue and discharges itself.

us_passport._why_this_entry_exists: As the control case. A document with no fiduciary and no debt-holder shows the model does not invent layers to fill its own shape.

assignment.note: Nothing to assign. A passport is issued to a person and evidences their nationality; it is not a transferable interest, and this entry is the control case showing the chain layer does not invent one.

usps_money_order.label: USPS money order

identifier.note: USPS is authorised to provide money orders.

holder.note: A money order is payable to a named payee and moves by endorsement, so WHO HOLDS IT NOW is a real question with a real answer - and it has not been checked for any particular instrument. Left empty for the same reason debt_holder is: this is the entry the 'postal trust account' claim turns on, and a plausible name here would manufacture the answer.

fiduciary.note: Whether USPS holds the funds in any fiduciary capacity or simply owes a debt on the instrument has NOT been checked. This is the field the 'postal trust account' claim turns on, so it is left empty deliberately.

debt_holder.note: LEFT EMPTY ON PURPOSE, and the CI gate caught it being filled. The ordinary reading is that USPS owes the face amount to the payee, but that is the reading, not the record - 39 CFR part 762 has not been opened. debt_holder is the one field somebody acts on, so a plausible entity here is worse than a blank one.

usps_money_order._note_on_the_trust_claim: A money order is recorded here because it is the instrument most often described as a 'postal trust account'. THIS ENTRY DOES NOT SUPPORT THAT DESCRIPTION AND DOES NOT REFUTE IT - two of five layers are unverified and the trace says so. Resolving it means reading 39 CFR part 762 and the DMM, which has not been done. An entry that guessed here would manufacture the answer the question exists to find.
usps_money_order._corrected: 2026-09-11: debt_holder had been filled with 'USPS' while marked unverified. That is the exact shape this schema exists to prevent and the gate failed on it.

assignment.note: Negotiation by endorsement is how the interest moves, and 39 CFR part 762 has not been opened. not_checked rather than never_existed: this instrument CAN be transferred, so an empty chain here means nobody looked.

va_disability_compensation.label: VA disability compensation

holder.note: The veteran holds the entitlement. 38 U.S.C. 5301(a)(1) makes payments of benefits due or to become due NOT ASSIGNABLE except as specifically authorized by law, and exempt from the claim of creditors before or after receipt. So this layer is not merely filled - it is FIXED, which no other layer in this schema is. The interest cannot be sold, pledged, or transferred, and a document purporting to do so does not move it.
holder.status_note: The entitlement runs while eligibility continues.

fiduciary.note: NONE BY DEFAULT. A VA fiduciary exists only where the Secretary finds a beneficiary unable to manage their own affairs and appoints one under 5502. Where one IS appointed the layer is filled with that person - and the appointment is the thing to read, not the label.
fiduciary.status_note: No fiduciary unless appointed under 38 U.S.C. 5502.

debt_holder.note: The obligation to pay runs from the United States to the veteran. An overpayment reverses it - 38 U.S.C. 5314 - and that is a different account, not this one.
debt_holder.status_note: The obligation runs while entitlement continues.

va_disability_compensation._why_this_entry_exists: The clean public case: benefit public, servicer public, obligation on the government. It is the baseline any privatised-benefit finding is measured against.

assignment.note: No chain can exist. Non-assignability is the statute's first sentence, so an empty trail here is a finding rather than a gap - which is the whole reason never_existed is a separate state from not_checked. 16 CFR 433 does not reach this account at all: there is no consumer credit contract and no seller.

_status_field: Every layer carries status: active / revoked / superseded / expired / unknown / never_existed. UNKNOWN IS THE DEFAULT AND IS NOT ACTIVE - a layer nobody checked must not read as binding. An appointment that has been revoked is the difference between a claim and a gift, and a map that shows structure without status points at dead appointments.
_schema_1_1: 1.1 adds the `holder` layer and the `assignment` block. The five earlier layers all asked who is DOING something to the account; nobody asked who OWNS the right to enforce it, because on a public benefit that answer is obvious and never moves. On assigned consumer paper it moves repeatedly and the party now demanding payment is routinely not the party the person dealt with. Every 1.0 entry was reread and given a holder rather than backfilled with a default - three of the five are honestly empty.
_holder_is_not_debt_holder: They are opposite sides and the name is a trap. `debt_holder` is who CARRIES the obligation - on a VA benefit, the United States; on a car note, the person. `holder` is who may enforce it and be paid. Ordinary usage of 'holds the debt' means the second, and this schema has always meant the first, so it is written down in both places rather than renamed under five entries and a build gate.
_assignment: A chain of who held the interest, each link recorded from a document. A link exists because an instrument says so - never because an entity is the usual assignee for that kind of paper. `holder_rule_notice` records whether the contract carries the notice 16 CFR 433.2 requires, which is what decides whether claims and defenses ride the assignment, and which also caps recovery at amounts the debtor actually paid. It is recorded, never inferred from the kind of account.
_personal_entries_are_not_here: Entries describing the principal's own holdings live in private/account_layers.private.json, which .gitignore excludes, and are merged at load. This file is the SCHEMA plus generic instruments used as control cases - a passport and a money order, which name nobody. A reader can audit every rule here without learning one true fact about the principal's finances.
